source.prompt: What CRM should a marketing agency use to manage client pipelines?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Marketing agencies benefit most from CRMs that combine visual pipeline management, project delivery integration, and marketing automation—top choices include HubSpot, Insightly, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, and Monday CRM.
Key Considerations for Agencies
When selecting a CRM, marketing agencies should prioritize:
Pipeline visibility: Clear stages for tracking deals from lead to close.
Project delivery integration: Systems that transition smoothly from sales to project execution.
Marketing automation: Tools for lead nurturing, email campaigns, and workflows.
Collaboration and integrations: Connect with email, calendar, project management, accounting, and creative tools without redundant data entry.
Budget and scalability: Fits agency size and growth plans.
Top CRM Options for Marketing Agencies
1. HubSpot CRM – Best for inbound marketing agencies Insightly+1
Integrated contact management, email automation, landing pages, and lead nurturing in one platform.
Strong reporting dashboards and AI-powered content suggestions.
Free tier available; paid plans scale to enterprise features.
Ideal for agencies whose primary focus is marketing campaigns over project delivery.
2. Insightly – Best for agencies balancing sales and project delivery Insightly
Native deal-to-project conversion preserves client history after a deal closes.
Built-in project management alongside sales pipeline.
Excellent for creative and digital agencies needing visibility across both sales and delivery.
Supports 2,000+ integrations for easy connection to existing tools.
3. Pipedrive – Best for sales-focused teams Insightly+2
Visual, drag-and-drop Kanban pipeline emphasizes deal tracking.
Activity-based selling with reminders and task tracking.
Extra project management may require additional tools.
Suitable for agencies prioritizing business development and lead follow-up.
4. Zoho CRM – Best for budget-conscious agencies Insightly+1
Offers free plan for up to 3 users and competitive paid tiers.
Supports forecasting, lead nurturing, workflows, and broad integration within Zoho apps.
Ideal for small agencies seeking solid CRM functionality without premium costs.
5. Monday CRM – Best for project-first teams Insightly+1
Combines visual boards of projects and sales pipelines.
Supports automations and dashboards for tracking deals and activities.
Works well for agencies already using Monday for project management, though CRM functionality is lighter than dedicated platforms.
Other Notable Options
OneSuite: All-in-one CRM, invoicing, and client portal for small service agencies, offering an integrated Kanban pipeline 1.
ActiveCampaign: Strong in automated customer journeys and marketing automation.
Salesforce: Highly customizable enterprise-level workflows but requires setup expertise and higher cost 1.
ClickUp / Freshworks / Agile CRM / Copper: Useful depending on existing tools and focus on integrations, but may require additional modules for project delivery or advanced marketing automation 2.
Choosing the Right CRM for Your Agency
Identify where client workflow difficulties occur: is it lead tracking, project handoffs, or marketing campaigns?
Match the CRM’s strengths to your agency’s priorities. For example, choose Insightly for strong sales-to-project handoff or HubSpot for inbound campaign support.
Consider team size, budget, integration needs, and ease of adoption to minimize disruption during implementation.
By evaluating your agency’s workflow bottlenecks, you can select a CRM that not only tracks pipelines but also enhances client delivery and marketing performance Insightly+2.
